- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is rising steadily, cap the upward slope to avoid overshoot after spikes.
- If supply net is strongly bearish (net < -15) and true outcome shows sharp declines, reduce forecast slope to avoid lagged overcorrection.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >75), model tends to overcorrect downward — apply a 1-2 day lagged decay to prevent premature reversal.
- When bullish sentiment is high but true outcome is volatile or mean-reverting, reduce forecast momentum by 10-15% to account for sentiment overreaction.
- If event count is high and supply net is negative, forecast should be slightly below historical mean to reflect supply constraint bias.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is mixed or neutral, model should not assume trend continuation — use 2-3 day smoothing to avoid false momentum.
